title: kv-cache-attn-seqlen-debug-scratchpad-17
content:
Background:
Investigating intermittent correctness regressions when serving long-context requests (seqlen boundary cases) - observed mismatched logits / token divergence after ~1k-2k tokens in a subset of requests. Behavior more common on mixed-batch traffic that mixes short (<=256) and long (>=2048) requests.

Symptoms seen (examples):
- Repro script: tools/repro/run_repro.py --model rwd-v1-7B --device a100:0 --batch-sizes 1,4 --seq-len 3072 --prefill 1536
- Error snippet from runtime log: "ASSERT kv_cache_idx == expected_idx (step=1024): expected=2048 got=2049"
- Downstream: token divergence at step ~1102 (gold token id 345 vs produced 348).
- Observed with int8/ptq configs and fp16; more frequently when using grouped-quantization profile gpq-v2.

Commands/traces tried so far:
- Local reproduce (single GPU): python -m repro.run_repro --config tests/long_seq.yaml  (consistent ~40% flaky reproduces)
- Added extra checks in runtime to dump kv_cache slice at boundary:  x86 binary symbolized via addr2line, compared keys/values across steps.
- Ran with ASAN build (serving-runtime/asan) - no heap corruption reported.
- Forced kernel selection to "flash-attn" and "gemm-based" via env SERVE_FORCE_KERNEL=flash|gemm, behavior differs: flash-attn seems to reduce frequency but not eliminate.
- Tried single-request stress with dynamic batching off (SERVE_BATCHING=0) -> largely stable.
- Bisected PRs: revert of PR#1820 (kv-cache compact rewrite) reduces incidence but doesn't fully remove. PR#1820 probably exposed but not sole cause.

Hypotheses:
1) Off-by-one in kv-cache write index when attention kernel path changes mid-request due to dynamic batch merging. Kernel A writes with stride S1, kernel B expects S2 -> misaligned read at boundary.
2) Padding/strip handling: when inputs with different prefix lengths are merged, pad tokens aren't getting correctly masked in kv cache flush/restore for some quantized kernels.
3) Race in kernel selection: async compile+cache (kernel cache miss) triggers a short fallback kernel that uses a different ordering for KV store.
4) Quantization edge: grouped-quantized codepath packs keys differently (4x pack) and an alignment assumption fails for certain seqlen modulo values (> 2048).

Reproducer notes and easy checks:
- Deterministic reproducer (slow but helpful): 
  - start server with --disable-dynamic-batching --log-kv-checks
  - run repro/long_seq_repro.py with fixed seed 42 and compare token-by-token to baseline golden output.
- Quick diff: dump hex of kv_cache.key[step-2:step+2] for both flash and gemm when divergence occurs. Use repro/dump_kv.py which emits csv.

Immediate next steps / TODOs:
- (Ethan) Add stricter invariants on kv write/read index with optional kill-on-mismatch flag; log full slice every mismatch (low perf).
- (Maya) Add unit test that simulates mixed-batch merge: batch A len 256, batch B len 3072, run through kernel selection codepath and check kv offsets.
- (Priya) Audit kernel cache path for async fallback sequences; add metrics for kernel-selection changes mid-request.
- Try repro on older runtime (pre-PR#1820) and on latest master with new quant fixes (PR#1892) to narrow down.

Notes / breadcrumbs from today's runs:
- 2024-11-09 13:14 UTC - run #276: divergence at step 1102, SERVE_FORCE_KERNEL=gemm -> mismatch present.
- 2024-11-10 09:42 UTC - run #329: SERVE_FORCE_KERNEL=flash -> no mismatch, but dev profiler shows extra memcpy at kv flush boundary.
- 2024-11-11 17:03 UTC - ASAN build run -> no heap issues; suggests logical/state bug not memory corruption.

Possible mitigations (short-term):
- Disable dynamic merging of short+long requests at the routing layer until invariants confirmed. Adds tail-latency hit for throughput but improves correctness. (config toggle).
- When selecting kernel, ensure canonical ordering/serialization of KV writes (i.e., kernel switch must flush and rebase kv_index).

References / links (local):
- repro scripts: tools/repro/long_seq_repro.py
- kv dump helper: tools/repro/dump_kv.py
- suspected PR: github PR #1892 (quant fixes), PR #1820 (kv compact rewrite)

Open questions to answer in follow-ups:
- Does the issue correlate with specific CUDA driver versions or only with mixed quant profiles? (test matrix pending)
- Are there any off-by-one arithmetic ops in the grouped-quant code that assume 64-byte alignment?

Short-term plan: finish the unit test for mixed-batch merge (Maya), land extra kv index assertion/logging (Ethan) behind flag, run full repro matrix across kernels/drivers by EoWeek.

Scratchpad raw dumps (attached locally):
- /tmp/kv-dumps/run_329_gemm_kv_slice_1100.csv
- /tmp/kv-dumps/run_276_flash_kv_slice_1100.csv

If anyone picks this up: start by running repro with --log-kv-checks and attach the CSVs to RI-3421. The mismatch row usually shows a one-token shift in the keys around the seqlen boundary.
